e: Uber announces the immediate closure of its ride-hailing in Uganda, ending its operations in the country after beginning there in 2016.
Uganda authorizes deploying its soldiers for the International Stabilization Force in Gaza.
A taxi van and a truck collide in Kalungu District, killing 14 people.
Uganda inaugurates Yonatan Netanyahu's statue as a honour at Entebbe International Airport.
A school bus returning from an educational trip to Sipi Falls crashes in Kapchorwa District, killing 21 people.
At least 16 people die of starvation in the Karamoja sub-region following a prolonged drought that destroyed crops.

A group of Ugandan farmers file a case in the UK High Court against the East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP), seeking to apply Ugandan constitutional, environmental, and climate law to the project.

General Muhoozi Kainerugaba orders the closure of the Daily Monitor and NTV Uganda, stating that he does not believe in a free press. Military personnel are deployed to the media groups' premises in Kampala.
Opposition politician Erias Lukwago is arrested by soldiers after pursuing a case against army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba.
A minivan carrying personnel from the Uganda Revenue Authority collides with an elephant inside Murchison Falls National Park, killing three passengers.
The government issues a temporary ban on handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact in response to the 2026 Ituri Province Ebola epidemic.
President Museveni signs the Protection of Sovereignty Bill into law, forbidding foreign interference in the country.
The Ugandan Health Ministry confirms an outbreak of Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease, after a Congolese patient dies in intensive care in Kampala.
Yoweri Museveni is inaugurated to a seventh term as president.
Authorities announce the detention of 231 foreign nationals following two operations against human trafficking and online scams.
Four children are killed in a mass stabbing at a school in Kampala. The perpetrator, an adult man, is arrested and sentenced to death on 30 April.
The southern white rhinoceros is reintroduced at Kidepo Valley National Park for the first time since being poached into extinction at the park in 1983.
Opposition leader Bobi Wine announces his departure from Uganda after having gone into hiding since the presidential election in January.
Uganda announces visa-free entry to nationals of 40 countries.
Five people are killed and 11 others are injured when a bus collides with a truck on the Kampala–Gulu Highway near Bweyale Town, Kiryandongo District.
Jacob Kiplimo sets a new men’s half-marathon world record of 57:20 in Lisbon, improving his previous record by 10 seconds.
Police in Arua arrest two women on allegations of engaging in same-sex acts, after they were reportedly seen kissing in public, in violation of the Anti-Homosexuality Act, 2023.
Opposition MP Muwanga Kivumbi is arrested on charges related to the clashes in Butambala on 16 January.
Authorities partially restore internet services following President Museveni’s election victory, allowing business use while keeping social media blocked.
At least seven people are killed in clashes between police and opposition supporters in Butambala District following the general election.
The Uganda Communications Commission imposes a suspension of mobile internet services, citing misinformation, electoral fraud and incitement of violence.
The government bans live broadcasts and streaming of riots, unlawful processions, and violent incidents ahead of the presidential election.
